deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing Art. 4 of Gauss's Nachlass essay on biquadratic residues). The modulus is m = ε(a+bi), where ε>0 is the gcd of the two components of m and gcd(a,b)=1. Write N = a²+b²; the page writes e for ε. The quarter system k (Viertelsystem, the quartic analogue of the half-system in Gauss's lemma) was defined on the previous page. It consists of the Gaussian integers x+iy with 0 < ax+by < εN/2 and 0 ≤ ay−bx < εN/2.

(1) Boundary members. The page completes the previous page's count of members with ay−bx = 0. Since gcd(a,b)=1, these are x+iy = t(a+bi) with t real, and then ax+by = tN. So 0 < t < ε/2, i.e. t = 1, 2, ..., (ε−1)/2 (ε odd, implicit). There are (ε−1)/2 such members, and none when ε = 1.

(2) The four quarter systems. Put k' = ik, k'' = −k, k''' = −ik. Equivalently, using representatives shifted by multiples of m: k' = m+ik, k'' = (1+i)m − k, k''' = im − ik.

Coordinates (my addition). Write 2f/m = ξ+iη. Since (x+iy)(a−bi) = (ax+by) + i(ay−bx), we get ξ = 2(ax+by)/(εN) and η = 2(ay−bx)/(εN). The residues mod m correspond to (ξ,η) mod 2, i.e. to a 2×2 square.
- k = {0<ξ<1, 0≤η<1}.
- k' = m+ik: (ξ,η) → (2−η, ξ), so ξ∈(1,2], η∈(0,1).
- k'' = (1+i)m−k: (2−ξ, 2−η), so ξ∈(1,2), η∈(1,2].
- k''' = im−ik: (η, 2−ξ), so ξ∈[0,1), η∈(1,2).
These four regions tile (0,2]×(0,2] minus the corners, i.e. all residues not divisible by m.

(3) Decision rule. Given x+iy not divisible by m, write 2(ax+by) = P·εN + Q and 2(ay−bx) = R·εN + S with P, Q, R, S real integers, normalised by the table:
- k: P even, R even, 0<Q<εN, 0≤S<εN.
- k': P odd, R even, 0<Q≤εN, 0<S<εN.
- k'': P odd, R odd, 0<Q<εN, 0<S≤εN.
- k''': P even, R odd, 0≤Q<εN, 0<S<εN.
This is just the coordinate description in (2), with P = integer part of ξ and R = integer part of η.

(4) Simplification by cases.

Case I: neither ax+by nor ay−bx is divisible by εN. Since εN is odd (implicit: m odd), ξ and η are non-integers. Take P = ⌊ξ⌋ and R = ⌊η⌋. Then the parities give the class:
- (even, even) → k
- (odd, even) → k'
- (odd, odd) → k''
- (even, odd) → k'''

Case II: εN | ax+by. Then ay−bx is divisible by N but not by εN, hence 2(ay−bx) is not divisible by εN either (marginal addition).
- Divisibility by N (my filling-in): b(ax+by) + a(ay−bx) = Ny, and gcd(a,N) = 1.
- Not by εN: otherwise εN divides (x+iy)(a−bi), so m | x+iy.
Here ξ is an even integer, i.e. ξ ≡ 0 mod 2. The point lies on the edge ξ = 2 of k' (η∈(0,1)) or the edge ξ = 0 of k''' (η∈(1,2)). Hence R = ⌊η⌋ even gives k', R odd gives k'''.

Case III (continued on next page) is the symmetric case: εN | ay−bx. Then P = ⌊ξ⌋ even gives k, odd gives k''.

Purpose: this classification feeds Art. 5 (next page). There the biquadratic character of M with respect to m is computed by a Gauss-lemma count Σψ(f) mod 4, with ψ read off from ⌊ξ⌋, ⌊η⌋ of 2fM/m.
errors: No mathematical errors found; I checked every table entry against the coordinate description.

Implicit assumption: ε (indeed εN) is odd. This is needed for the count (ε−1)/2 and for '2(ax+by) divisible by εN iff ax+by divisible by εN'. It is stated explicitly only on the next page ('ungeraden Modulus').
The claim in II that N divides ay−bx is stated without proof. It is true, via b(ax+by)+a(ay−bx) = N·y and gcd(a,N) = 1.
The normalisation of P, Q, R, S is ambiguous when Q or S could be 0 or εN. Gauss's table resolves this per class, so the rule is consistent but the cases must be read jointly.

results.what: Explicit fundamental 'quarter system' k for Z[i]/(m), m = ε(a+bi), and its rotations k', k'', k''' tiling the nonzero residues. Includes the boundary-point count (ε−1)/2.
results.modern_name: Quarter-system (Viertelsystem) for the quartic Gauss lemma: a set of representatives of (Z[i]/m)^× modulo the units {±1, ±i}
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, published in Werke II); the quartic Gauss lemma was later used by Eisenstein (1844) and Busche

results.what: Criterion deciding which quarter system a residue x+iy lies in, via the integer parts and parities of 2(ax+by)/(εN) and 2(ay−bx)/(εN). Includes the boundary cases where one coordinate is divisible by εN.
results.modern_name: Lattice-point / floor-function evaluation of the quartic Gauss lemma (coordinates of 2f/m)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Werke II, Nachlass on biquadratic residues); cf. Eisenstein, Busche

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Gauss's known Nachlass treatment of biquadratic residues via a Gauss-lemma analogue with quarter systems, edited in Werke II. The page is careful bookkeeping (boundary cases, parity table) rather than a new result.

checkable.asserts: (x+iy)·conj(a+bi) = (ax+by) + i(ay−bx); gives ξ, η coordinates of 2f/m. Should be 0.
Identity behind Case II: N | ax+by implies N | ay−bx when gcd(a,b)=1. Should be 0.
k' = m+ik maps 2f/m = ξ+iη to (2−η) + iξ. Should be 0.
k'' = (1+i)m − k maps (ξ,η) to (2−ξ, 2−η). Should be 0.
k''' = im − ik maps ξ+iη to η + i(2−ξ). Should be 0.
